docs.title: Welcome to GraphAide
docs.text:
GraphAide is a multi-agentic platform for building intelligent applications powered by Large Language Models (LLMs). Knowledge graph construction is one powerful example—transforming documents into queryable knowledge graphs by extracting entities and relationships. But GraphAide's capabilities extend far beyond KGs.

Whether you work with PDFs, text files, images, or web data, GraphAide can: - Extract structured information and entities from any source - Process diverse data with multiple LLM providers and models - Ground information to external knowledge bases and sources - Build intelligent workflows with minimal setup - Track data provenance and attribution throughout - Scale from single documents to large datasets

docs.title: Why GraphAide?
docs.text: Capability Benefit Flexible LLM Support Use OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, AWS Bedrock, or local models—choose what works for you Extensible Architecture Build custom agents and workflows beyond KG construction Multi-Retriever RAG Combine multiple knowledge sources for richer, more accurate results Any Data Source Extract from PDFs, text, images, APIs, databases, or web data Production Ready Deploy as CLI, Docker, Python library, REST API, or embedded Enterprise Grade Track provenance, ensure compliance, audit all operations

docs.title: Setup Virtual Environment (Recommended)
docs.text:
Before installing GraphAide, create an isolated environment to manage dependencies:

Option 1: Using uv (Fastest) ⚡ 

uv venv graphaide-env
# On macOS/Linux:
source graphaide-env/bin/activate
# On Windows:
graphaide-env\Scripts\activate

Option 2: Using Conda 

conda create -n graphaide python=3.12
conda activate graphaide

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
1. Install GraphAide (latest version 0.6.7):

We recommend uv for fast, reliable installation: 

uv pip install graphaide==0.6.7

Or use pip: 

pip install graphaide==0.6.7

2. Extract knowledge graph: 

from graphaide import GraphAide, ModelConfig, get_sample_data_path

# Initialize GraphAide with your LLM
graphaide = GraphAide(
    model_config=ModelConfig(
        provider="openai", 
        model_name="gpt-5.6-luna",
        api_key="..."
    )
)

# Extract from sample document
sample_pdf = get_sample_data_path("PNNL_About.pdf")
sample_ontology = get_sample_data_path("ontology_cyber.nt")
result = graphaide.extract(file_path=sample_pdf, ontology_path=sample_ontology)
print(f"✓ Extracted {len(result.nodes)} entities, {len(result.edges)} relationships")

docs.title: Use Case 2: Build Knowledge Graph from Multiple Documents
docs.text:
import os
from graphaide import GraphAide, ModelConfig

graphaide = GraphAide(
    model_config=ModelConfig(provider="openai", model_name="gpt-5.6-luna", api_key="...")
)

# Ingest all PDFs
for filename in os.listdir("documents/"):
    if filename.endswith(".pdf"):
        print(f"Ingesting {filename}...")
        graphaide.ingest(file_path=f"documents/{filename}")

# Query
answer = graphaide.query("What are the main topics?")
print(answer)

docs.title: Use Case 4: Semantic Search with Vector Store
docs.text:
from graphaide import GraphAide, ModelConfig, VectorDBConfig
from graphaide.workflows.schemas import VectorStoreConfig

graphaide = GraphAide(
    model_config=ModelConfig(provider="openai", model_name="gpt-5.6-luna", api_key="..."),
    vectordb_config=VectorDBConfig(provider="chromadb", path="./kb")
)

# Build knowledge base
graphaide.ingest_to_vectordb(file_paths=["knowledge.pdf"], split_docs=True)

# Extract with context
result = graphaide.extract(
    file_path="new_document.pdf",
    vector_stores=[
        VectorStoreConfig(
            type="chromadb",
            path="./kb",
            retrieve_type="documents"
        )
    ]
)

docs.title: Use Case 5: Batch Process JSONL
docs.text:
from graphaide import GraphAide, ModelConfig

graphaide = GraphAide(
    model_config=ModelConfig(provider="openai", model_name="gpt-5.6-luna", api_key="...")
)

# documents.jsonl: {"text": "document content"}
result = graphaide.ingest(
    jsonl_file_path="documents.jsonl",
    jsonl_field_name="text",
    jsonl_lines_per_batch=4
)

print(f"Processed {result.segments_processed} documents")

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Term Definition Entity A specific thing extracted (person, organization, location, etc.) Relationship A connection between two entities (works for, located in, etc.) Ontology A formal definition of entity and relationship types for a domain Embedding Numerical representation of text for semantic search Vector Store Database of embeddings for fast semantic retrieval RAG Retrieval-Augmented Generation (using external knowledge during generation) Knowledge Graph A graph of interconnected entities and relationships LLM Large Language Model (AI model like GPT-4, Claude) Neo4j Popular graph database for storing knowledge graphs

docs.title: Context Window Size
docs.text:
Control how much text is processed per segment:

result = graphaide.extract(
    file_path="document.pdf",
    max_tokens_per_segment=8192,  # Options: 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768
    context_window_mode="medium"
)

Presets: - small (4096) — For resource-limited deployments - medium (8192) — Balanced, supports richer context - large (16384) — For models like GPT-4 and Claude 3 - xlarge (32768) — For cutting-edge models with massive windows

docs.text:

docs.title: Knowledge Graph Extraction
docs.text: Learn how to automatically extract entities and relationships from your documents.

docs.title: What is Extraction?
docs.text:
Extraction is the process of analyzing a document and identifying:

  • Entities — Things like people, organizations, locations, concepts
  • Relationships — Connections between entities (e.g., "works for", "located in")

GraphAide uses LLMs to understand document context and extract this structured information.

docs.title: Quick Start: Extract from a PDF
Simplest Example
docs.text:
from graphaide import GraphAide, ModelConfig, get_sample_data_path

graphaide = GraphAide(
    model_config=ModelConfig(
        provider="openai",
        model_name="gpt-5.6-luna",
        api_key="..."
    )
)

# Extract entities and relationships
result = graphaide.extract(file_path="document.pdf")

print(f"Found {len(result.nodes)} entities")
print(f"Found {len(result.edges)} relationships")

# View extracted data
for node in result.nodes:
    print(f"- {node.label}: {node.properties}")

docs.title: Access Extracted Data
docs.text:
result = graphaide.extract(file_path="document.pdf")

# Nodes (entities)
for node in result.nodes:
    print(f"Type: {node.type}")
    print(f"Label: {node.label}")
    print(f"Properties: {node.properties}")

# Edges (relationships)
for edge in result.edges:
    print(f"Relationship: {edge.type}")
    print(f"From: {edge.source} → To: {edge.target}")
    print(f"Properties: {edge.properties}")

docs.title: Filter by Ontology
docs.text:
Keep only entities and relationships that match your ontology:

result = graphaide.extract(
    file_path="document.pdf",
    ontology_path="ontology.nt",
    filter_by_ontology=True  # Only keep types defined in ontology

docs.title: Merge Results
docs.text:
Automatically deduplicate and consolidate extracted data:

result = graphaide.extract(
    file_path="document.pdf",
    merge_output=True  # Combine duplicate entities
)

docs.title: Processing Steps
docs.text:
Here's what GraphAide does internally:

1. Load Document
   ↓
2. Split into Segments (chunks)
   ↓
3. For Each Segment:
   - Retrieve Context (from Vector Store/Ontology)
   - Send to LLM for Extraction
   - Parse Entities & Relationships
   ↓
4. Combine Results
   ↓
5. Save to JSON

docs.title: Using Ontologies in Extraction
docs.text: Learn how to guide GraphAide extraction with domain-specific ontologies.

docs.title: What is an Ontology?
docs.text:
An ontology defines:

  • Entity Types — What things exist in your domain (e.g., Person, Organization, Technology)
  • Relationship Types — How things connect (e.g., "works for", "uses", "develops")
  • Properties — Characteristics of entities and relationships

It acts as a blueprint that tells GraphAide: "Look for these specific types of information."

docs.title: Why Use Ontologies?
docs.text: Benefit Example Precision Extract only relevant entity types for your domain Consistency All extractions use the same vocabulary Quality LLM focuses on domain-specific patterns Filtering Automatically exclude irrelevant entities

docs.title: Ontology Formats
docs.text:
GraphAide supports standard semantic web formats:

  • N-Triples (.nt) — Simple, line-based RDF format
  • Turtle (.ttl) — More readable RDF format
  • OWL (.owl) — Complex ontology definitions

docs.title: Simple N-Triples Example
docs.text:
<http://example.org/Organization> <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type> <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#Class> .
<http://example.org/Person> <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type> <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#Class> .
<http://example.org/worksWith> <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type> <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#ObjectProperty> .

docs.title: Step 1: Define Entity Types
docs.text:
Think about what kinds of things exist in your domain:

- Person (people)
- Organization (companies, institutions)
- Technology (software, tools)
- Vulnerability (security issues)
- Tactic (attack methods)

docs.title: Step 2: Define Relationship Types
docs.text:
What connections matter?

- develops (Person develops Technology)
- worksFor (Person worksFor Organization)
- affects (Vulnerability affects Technology)
- uses (Organization uses Technology)

docs.title: Step 3: Write N-Triples Ontology
docs.text:
# Entity Types
<http://example.org/Person> <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type> <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#Class> .
<http://example.org/Organization> <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type> <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#Class> .
<http://example.org/Technology> <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type> <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#Class> .

# Relationship Types
<http://example.org/worksFor> <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type> <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#ObjectProperty> .
<http://example.org/develops> <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type> <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#ObjectProperty> .
<http://example.org/uses> <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type> <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#ObjectProperty> .

docs.title: Step 4: Use It
docs.text:
result = graphaide.extract(
    file_path="document.pdf",
    ontology_path="my_ontology.nt"
)

docs.title: Generate Ontology Automatically
docs.text:
If you don't have an ontology, let GraphAide create one:

result = graphaide.generate_ontology(
    node_types=["Person", "Organization", "Technology"],
    edge_types=["worksFor", "develops", "uses"],
    output_path="generated_ontology.nt"
)

    "worksFor", "manages", "develops", 
    "competes_with", "located_in"
]

result = graphaide.generate_ontology(
    node_types=ontology_types,
    edge_types=ontology_rels,
    output_path="business_ontology.nt"
)

docs.title: Ingesting Knowledge Graphs to Neo4j
docs.text: Learn how to load extracted data into Neo4j for querying and analysis.

docs.title: What is Ingestion?
docs.text: Ingestion is the process of taking extracted entities and relationships and loading them into a Neo4j graph database, where you can query and analyze them.

docs.title: Configure Neo4j Connection
docs.text:
First, set up your Neo4j database configuration:

from graphaide import GraphDBConfig

graphdb_config = GraphDBConfig(
    uri="neo4j://localhost:7687",      # Neo4j server address
    username="neo4j",                   # Neo4j username
    password="password"                 # Neo4j password
)

docs.title: Initialize GraphAide with Neo4j
docs.text:
from graphaide import GraphAide, ModelConfig, GraphDBConfig

# Setup LLM
model_config = ModelConfig(
    provider="openai",
    model_name="gpt-5.6-luna",
    api_key="..."
)

# Setup Neo4j
graphdb_config = GraphDBConfig(
    uri="neo4j://localhost:7687",
    username="neo4j",
    password="password"
)

# Initialize GraphAide with both configs
graphaide = GraphAide(
    model_config=model_config,
    graphdb_config=graphdb_config
)

# Extract AND ingest to Neo4j in one call
result = graphaide.ingest(file_path="document.pdf")

print(f"✓ Ingested {result.nodes_created} entities")
print(f"✓ Ingested {result.edges_created} relationships")

docs.title: Ingest with Ontology
docs.text:
result = graphaide.ingest(
    file_path="document.pdf",
    ontology_path="ontology.nt"
)

docs.title: Ingest from Text
docs.text:
text = """
GraphAide is a knowledge graph system built by PNNL.
It uses LLMs to extract entities and relationships.
"""

result = graphaide.ingest(input_text=text)

docs.title: From JSONL File
docs.text:
Process many documents in parallel:

# documents.jsonl
# {"text": "First document content..."}
# {"text": "Second document content..."}
# {"text": "Third document content..."}

result = graphaide.ingest(
    jsonl_file_path="documents.jsonl",
    jsonl_field_name="text",
    jsonl_lines_per_batch=4  # Process 4 documents at once
)

print(f"Processed {result.segments_processed} documents")

docs.title: From Pre-extracted JSON
docs.text:
If you already have extracted data as JSON:

result = graphaide.load_json_to_neo4j(
    json_path="GraphAide_KG_Extract_20261014_120000.json"
)

print(f"Loaded {result.nodes_created} nodes")
print(f"Loaded {result.edges_created} edges")

docs.title: Clear Existing Graph
docs.text:
⚠️ Warning: This deletes all data in Neo4j!

result = graphaide.ingest(
    file_path="document.pdf",
    clear_existing=True  # Only use when intentional
)

docs.title: Filter by Ontology
docs.text:
Only ingest entities and relationships matching your ontology:

result = graphaide.ingest(
    file_path="document.pdf",
    ontology_path="ontology.nt",
    filter_by_ontology=True
)

docs.title: Ingestion Workflow
docs.text:
Here's what happens internally:

1. Extract Entities & Relationships
   ↓
2. Filter by Ontology (optional)
   ↓
3. Merge/Deduplicate (optional)
   ↓
4. Create Nodes in Neo4j
   ↓
5. Create Edges (Relationships) in Neo4j
   ↓
6. Return Statistics

docs.title: Build Knowledge Graph from Corpus
docs.text:
import os
from graphaide import GraphAide, ModelConfig

graphaide = GraphAide(
    model_config=ModelConfig(provider="openai", model_name="gpt-5.6-luna", api_key="...")
)

# Ingest all PDFs in folder
pdf_files = [f for f in os.listdir("documents/") if f.endswith(".pdf")]

for pdf_file in pdf_files:
    print(f"Ingesting {pdf_file}...")
    result = graphaide.ingest(file_path=f"documents/{pdf_file}")
    print(f"  → {result.nodes_created} entities, {result.edges_created} relationships")

docs.title: Iterative Refinement
docs.text:
# First pass: extract all
result1 = graphaide.ingest(file_path="doc.pdf", merge_output=False)

# Second pass: with ontology filtering
result2 = graphaide.ingest(
    file_path="doc.pdf",
    ontology_path="ontology.nt",
    filter_by_ontology=True
)

# Compare
print(f"Without filtering: {result1.nodes_created}")
print(f"With filtering: {result2.nodes_created}")

docs.title: Batch Processing with Error Handling
docs.text:
results = []

for jsonl_file in ["batch1.jsonl", "batch2.jsonl", "batch3.jsonl"]:
    try:
        result = graphaide.ingest(jsonl_file_path=jsonl_file)
        results.append({
            "file": jsonl_file,
            "nodes": result.nodes_created,
            "edges": result.edges_created
        })
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error ingesting {jsonl_file}: {e}")

# Summary
total_nodes = sum(r["nodes"] for r in results)
total_edges = sum(r["edges"] for r in results)
print(f"Total ingested: {total_nodes} nodes, {total_edges} edges")

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Get GraphAide running in minutes. Choose the method that works best for you.

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
• Python: 3.11 or later
  • Neo4j: 4.4 or later (optional for basic usage)
  • LLM API: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or AWS Bedrock account

docs.title: Setup Virtual Environment (Recommended)
docs.text:
Before installing GraphAide, create an isolated environment to manage dependencies:

Option 1: Using uv (Fastest) ⚡ 

uv venv graphaide-env
# On macOS/Linux:
source graphaide-env/bin/activate
# On Windows:
graphaide-env\Scripts\activate

Option 2: Using Conda 

conda create -n graphaide python=3.12
conda activate graphaide

docs.title: Method 1: uv (Recommended for Speed)
docs.text:
The fastest way to install GraphAide. We recommend uv for significantly faster dependency resolution:

uv pip install graphaide

Verify installation:

graphaide --version

docs.title: Method 2: pip
docs.text:
Standard Python package manager approach:

pip install graphaide

Verify installation:

graphaide --version

docs.title: Method 3: Using GraphAide as a Python Library
docs.text:
Use GraphAide programmatically in your Python code.

from graphaide import GraphAide, ModelConfig

graphaide = GraphAide(
    model_config=ModelConfig(
        provider="openai",
        model_name="gpt-5.6-luna",
        api_key="..."
    )
)

# Use GraphAide functions
result = graphaide.extract(file_path="document.pdf")

docs.title: Method 4: Docker
docs.text:
Run GraphAide in a containerized environment with all dependencies included.

git clone https://github.com/pnnl/GraphAide.git
cd GraphAide
docker compose up

Then access the REST API at http://localhost:8000.

docs.title: Method 5: Development Setup
docs.text:
For developers who want to contribute or modify GraphAide.

With uv (recommended): 

git clone https://github.com/pnnl/GraphAide.git
cd GraphAide
uv venv
# On macOS/Linux:
source .venv/bin/activate
# On Windows:
.venv\Scripts\activate
uv pip install -e ".[testing]"

Or with pip: 

git clone https://github.com/pnnl/GraphAide.git
cd GraphAide
pip install -e ".[testing]"

docs.title: Querying Your Knowledge Graph
docs.text: After ingesting data into Neo4j, query your knowledge graph using natural language with GraphAide.

docs.title: Using GraphAide Query
docs.text:
from graphaide import GraphAide, ModelConfig, GraphDBConfig

# Setup
graphaide = GraphAide(
    model_config=ModelConfig(
        provider="openai",
        model_name="gpt-5.6-luna",
        api_key="..."
    ),
    graphdb_config=GraphDBConfig(
        uri="neo4j://localhost:7687",
        username="neo4j",
        password="password"
    )
)

# Query your knowledge graph

result = graphaide.query("What organizations are mentioned?")
print(result.answer)

docs.title: Entity Queries
docs.text:
# Find all people
result = graphaide.query("Who are all the people mentioned?")
print(result.answer)

# Find specific relationships
result = graphaide.query("What companies does John Smith work for?")
print(result.answer)

# Find connected entities
result = graphaide.query("What projects are associated with AI research?")
print(result.answer)

docs.title: Relationship Queries
docs.text:
# Explore relationships
result = graphaide.query("What relationships exist between companies and technologies?")
print(result.answer)

# Find connections
result = graphaide.query("How are cybersecurity concepts connected?")
print(result.answer)

# Path finding
result = graphaide.query("What's the connection between AI and natural language processing?")
print(result.answer)

docs.title: Aggregation Queries
docs.text:
# Count entities
result = graphaide.query("How many different organizations are in the knowledge graph?")
print(result.answer)

# List operations
result = graphaide.query("List all the technologies mentioned and their uses")
print(result.answer)

# Statistical queries
result = graphaide.query("What are the most frequently mentioned concepts?")
print(result.answer)

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text:
The query() method accepts additional parameters:

result = graphaide.query(
    question="What organizations are mentioned?",
    log_level="DEBUG"  # Optional: Set logging level
)

docs.title: Query Process
docs.text:
Here's what happens internally when you query:

1. Intent Prediction
   - Determine if query is subjective, locality-based, or analytical
   ↓
2. Neo4j Cypher Generation
   - Generate Cypher query from natural language
   ↓
3. Vector Store Context (RAG)
   - Retrieve relevant document context if configured
   ↓
4. Graph Query Execution
   - Execute Cypher against Neo4j
   ↓
5. LLM Response Generation
   - Generate natural language answer with context
   ↓
6. Return Answer

docs.title: Query with Vector Store Context
docs.text:
If you've configured a vector store, queries automatically retrieve relevant document context:

from graphaide import GraphAide, ModelConfig, GraphDBConfig, VectorDBConfig

graphaide = GraphAide(
    model_config=ModelConfig(provider="openai", model_name="gpt-5.6-luna", api_key="..."),
    graphdb_config=GraphDBConfig(uri="neo4j://localhost:7687", username="neo4j", password="password"),
    vector_configs=VectorDBConfig(
        provider="chromadb",
        store_name="documents",
        store_path="./chroma"
    )
)

# Query now includes both graph data AND document context
result = graphaide.query("What specific technologies are mentioned for cybersecurity?")
print(result.answer)

docs.title: Understanding Query Results
docs.text:
The query result includes:

  • Answer: Natural language response to your question
  • Context: Relevant graph data and document passages
  • Confidence: How well the answer is grounded in the data
  • Sources: Where the information came from (nodes, documents)

docs.title: No Results from Query
docs.text:
Check that: 1. Data has been successfully ingested to Neo4j 2. Neo4j connection is working 3. Query is specific enough (avoid overly broad questions)

# Verify data exists
if graphaide.vector_configs:
    vector_config = graphaide.vector_configs if isinstance(graphaide.vector_configs, VectorDBConfig) else graphaide.vector_configs[0]
    doc_count = graphaide._get_vector_store_doc_count(vector_config)
else:
    doc_count = "N/A"
print(f"Documents in vector store: {doc_count}")

# Try a simpler query
result = graphaide.query("What entities are in the graph?")
print(result.answer)

docs.title: Query Execution Errors
docs.text:
# Enable debug logging to see detailed execution
result = graphaide.query(
    "Your question here?",
    log_level="DEBUG"
)
print(result.answer)

docs.title: Setting Up Vector Stores
docs.text: Learn how to load documents into vector stores for semantic retrieval during extraction.

docs.title: What is a Vector Store?
docs.text:
A vector store stores document chunks as embeddings (numerical representations). During extraction, it retrieves semantically relevant context to help the LLM make better decisions.

Why use it? Instead of sending the entire document, GraphAide can find the most relevant parts automatically.

docs.title: Quick Start: ChromaDB with Sample Data
Load Sample Documents into ChromaDB
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from graphaide import GraphAide, ModelConfig, VectorDBConfig, get_sample_data_path

# Setup LLM
model_config = ModelConfig(
    provider="openai",
    model_name="gpt-5.6-luna",
    api_key="..."
)

# Setup ChromaDB vector store with GVD name in home directory
home = Path.home()
vectordb_config = VectorDBConfig(
    provider="chromadb",
    store_name="GVD",
    store_path=str(home / "GVD")  # Path must be a string
)

graphaide = GraphAide(
    model_config=model_config,
    vector_configs=vectordb_config
)

# Load sample documents into vector store
cyber_file = get_sample_data_path("cyberkg.txt")
pdf_file = get_sample_data_path("PNNL_About.pdf")

result = graphaide.ingest_vectors(
    file_paths=[str(cyber_file), str(pdf_file)],
    split_docs=True,
    append=False
)

docs.title: Visualizing Vector Embeddings
docs.text: After loading documents into your vector store, you can inspect the vector space and create 2D visualizations using UMAP (Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection).

docs.title: Check Document Count and Visualize
docs.text:
from graphaide import GraphAide, ModelConfig, VectorDBConfig, get_sample_data_path
from pathlib import Path

# Check how many documents are stored
doc_count = graphaide._get_vector_store_doc_count(vectordb_config)
print(f"✓ Vector store contains {doc_count} documents")

# Create 2D UMAP projection and interactive visualization
viz_result = graphaide.project_vectors(
    output_dir="./visualizations",
    reuse_embedding=False,  # Compute new projection
    category_field="source"  # Color points by source document
)

print(f"✓ Projected {viz_result.stats['num_embeddings_projected']} embeddings")
print(f"✓ Visualization saved to: {viz_result.stats['visualization_image_path']}")

docs.title: Reuse Existing Projections
docs.text:
If you've already created a 2D projection and want to recreate the visualization with different settings:

# Reuse previous UMAP projection (faster, no recomputation)
viz_result = graphaide.project_vectors(
    output_dir="./visualizations",
    reuse_embedding=True,  # Skip UMAP, reuse .npy file
    save_png=True,  # Save as static PNG image
    category_field="metadata_filter"  # Different coloring
)

The visualization is interactive—hover over points to see metadata, zoom, pan, and toggle categories.

docs.title: Semantic Search with Reranking
docs.text: Query your vector store for semantically similar documents with optional FlashRank reranking to improve relevance.

docs.title: Query with Reranking (Recommended)
docs.text:
from graphaide import GraphAide, ModelConfig, VectorDBConfig
from pathlib import Path

home = Path.home()

graphaide = GraphAide(
    model_config=ModelConfig(
        provider="openai",
        model_name="gpt-5.6-luna",
        api_key="..."
    ),
    vector_configs=VectorDBConfig(
        provider="chromadb",
        store_name="GVD",
        store_path=str(home / "GVD")
    )
)

# Search with automatic FlashRank reranking (enabled by default)
result = graphaide.vector_query(
    query="What is cybersecurity?",
    topk=5,
    rerank=True  # Enable reranking for better relevance
)

# Results include both similarity and rerank scores
for doc in result["results"]:
    print(f"[{doc['rank']}] {doc['source']}")
    print(f"    Similarity: {doc['similarity_score']:.3f}")
    print(f"    Rerank: {doc['rerank_score']:.3f}")
    print(f"    Content: {doc['document'][:200]}...")
    print()

docs.title: Query without Reranking
docs.text:
# Disable reranking to use raw vector similarity
result = graphaide.vector_query(
    query="What is machine learning?",
    topk=5,
    rerank=False  # Use only vector similarity
)

docs.title: Via CLI
docs.text:
# Search with reranking
graphaide vector-query "What is data science?" --topk 5 --rerank

# Search without reranking
graphaide vector-query "What is data science?" --topk 5 --no-rerank

Result Structure: - rank: Document rank (1 = most relevant) - document: Document content preview - source: Source file or document name - title: Document title (if available) - page: Page number (if available) - similarity_score: Vector similarity score (0-1) - rerank_score: FlashRank relevance score (only if rerank=True)

docs.title: With Store Name and Path (Recommended)

home = Path.home()
VectorDBConfig(

    store_name="GVD",
    store_path=str(home / "GVD")  # Path must be a string

docs.title: Create Multiple Named Stores
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path

home = Path.home()

# Store 1: Cybersecurity knowledge (GVD)
gvd_config = VectorDBConfig(
    store_name="GVD",
    store_path=home / "GVD"
)

# Store 2: General knowledge
general_config = VectorDBConfig(
    store_name="general",
    store_path=home / "general"
)

# Load different data into each
graphaide1 = GraphAide(..., vector_configs=gvd_config)

    file_paths=[get_sample_data_path("cyberkg.txt")],
    append=False
)

graphaide2 = GraphAide(..., vector_configs=general_config)
graphaide2.ingest_vectors(
    file_paths=[get_sample_data_path("PNNL_About.pdf")],
    append=False
)

docs.title: Embedding Models
docs.text: Embeddings convert text into vectors. GraphAide supports:

    provider="openai",
    model_name="gpt-5.6-luna",
    embedding_model="text-embedding-3-small",
    api_key="..."

docs.title: Sentence Transformers (Local)
docs.text:

docs.title: Using Vector Stores in Extraction
docs.text: Learn how to enhance extraction with semantic search from vector stores.

docs.title: Why Use Vector Stores in Extraction?
docs.text:
During extraction, GraphAide can automatically retrieve relevant context from your vector store:

  • Better Decisions — LLM sees related entities and patterns
  • Consistency — Extracted entities match existing ones in your knowledge base
  • Efficiency — No need to manually provide context
  • Scale — Handle thousands of documents automatically

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
from graphaide import GraphAide, ModelConfig, VectorDBConfig

# First, load documents into vector store
graphaide = GraphAide(
    model_config=ModelConfig(provider="openai", model_name="gpt-5.6-luna", api_key="..."),
    vectordb_config=VectorDBConfig(provider="chromadb", path="./chroma")
)

# Load your knowledge base
graphaide.ingest_to_vectordb(
    file_paths=["knowledge_base.pdf"],
    split_docs=True
)

# Now extract from new documents, using knowledge base for context
result = graphaide.extract(
    file_path="new_document.pdf",
    # Vector store is automatically used for context retrieval
)

print(f"Extracted with context: {len(result.nodes)} entities")

docs.title: Specify Vector Store Behavior
docs.text:
from graphaide.workflows.schemas import VectorStoreConfig

result = graphaide.extract(
    file_path="document.pdf",
    vector_stores=[
        VectorStoreConfig(
            type="chromadb",
            path="./chroma",
            collection_name="documents",
            retrieve_type="entities",  # Retrieve similar entities
            description="Entity knowledge base"
        )
    ]
)

docs.title: Complete Example: Extraction with Vector Store
Step 1: Build Knowledge Base
docs.text:
from graphaide import GraphAide, ModelConfig, VectorDBConfig

graphaide = GraphAide(
    model_config=ModelConfig(provider="openai", model_name="gpt-5.6-luna", api_key="..."),
    vectordb_config=VectorDBConfig(provider="chromadb", path="./kb")
)

# Load reference documents
print("Building knowledge base...")
result = graphaide.ingest_to_vectordb(
    file_paths=[
        "company_structure.pdf",
        "personnel_list.txt",
        "technology_stack.pdf"
    ],
    split_docs=True
)

print(f"Knowledge base ready: {result.chunks_created} chunks")

docs.title: Step 2: Extract from New Document with Context
docs.text:
from graphaide.workflows.schemas import VectorStoreConfig

# Extract new document, using knowledge base for context
result = graphaide.extract(
    file_path="meeting_notes.pdf",
    vector_stores=[
        VectorStoreConfig(
            type="chromadb",
            path="./kb",
            collection_name="langchain",  # Default collection name
            retrieve_type="documents",
            description="Company knowledge base with context"
        )
    ]
)

print(f"Extracted: {len(result.nodes)} entities, {len(result.edges)} relationships")

docs.title: Step 3: Verify Results
docs.text:
# Check if extraction used context effectively
for node in result.nodes[:5]:
    print(f"- {node.label} ({node.type})")
    if node.properties:
        print(f"  Properties: {node.properties}")

docs.title: Combining Vector Stores with Ontology
docs.text:
Use ontology + vector stores together for maximum guidance:

result = graphaide.extract(
    file_path="document.pdf",
    ontology_path="ontology.nt",           # Define types
    vector_stores=[                         # Provide context
        VectorStoreConfig(
            type="chromadb",
            path="./chroma",
            retrieve_type="entities",
            description="Known entities matching ontology"
        )
    ],
    filter_by_ontology=True                # Keep only ontology types
)

docs.title: Control Retrieval Amount
docs.text:
# More retrieval = slower but better context
VectorStoreConfig(
    type="chromadb",
    path="./chroma",
    retrieve_type="documents",
    description="Full document context"  # Larger chunks retrieved
)

# Less retrieval = faster but less context
VectorStoreConfig(
    type="chromadb",
    path="./chroma",
    retrieve_type="entities",
    description="Just entity mentions"  # Smaller, focused retrieval
)

docs.title: Batch Processing with Vector Stores
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path

# Process multiple documents
docs = list(Path("documents").glob("*.pdf"))

for doc in docs:
    print(f"Processing {doc.name}...")

    result = graphaide.extract(
        file_path=str(doc),
        vector_stores=[
            VectorStoreConfig(
                type="chromadb",
                path="./kb",
                retrieve_type="documents"
            )
        ]
    )

    print(f"  → {len(result.nodes)} entities extracted")

Vector store retrieval may return different results for similar queries. To improve consistency:

    vector_stores=[VectorStoreConfig(   # Examples

        path="./chroma",

)
